parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: It contains 70 questions and each question carries 1 mark. Use the SCANTRON ANSWER SHEET for this part and blacken the letter of your choice with a pencil and make it bold.

parts.title: Part II – Filling blank Spaces
parts.instructions: Contains 5 questions and each question carries 1 mark. Write your answer on the separate answer sheet provided.

parts.title: Part III – Matching
parts.instructions: It contains 10 questions and each question carries 1 point. Match column A with column B.

parts.title: Part IV – Short answer questions
parts.instructions: It contains 5 questions and each question carries 3 points. Write your answer on the separate answer sheet provided.

questions.stem: Explain the differences between Athens and Sparta.
questions.answer: Athens was a naval, commercial democracy that valued philosophy, arts and debate. Sparta was a land-based oligarchy/military state that trained citizen-soldiers (agoge) and used helot labour. Athens opened citizenship to debate; Sparta restricted power to equals (homoioi) and feared helot revolt.
explanation_steps: Contrast government, economy, culture and military
questions.marking_points: 1 mark government (democracy vs oligarchy/military state); 1 mark economy/military (navy/trade vs army/helots); 1 mark culture or education (philosophy vs agoge).
tips: Always pair one Athens trait with the Spartan opposite.

questions.stem: Mention the objectives of ELM (Haraka).
questions.answer: ELM/Haraka aimed to end Ethiopian annexation by clandestine political work, to unite Christians and Muslims, and to prepare the ground for organised resistance without an immediate full-scale guerrilla army. It recruited in towns and among students and workers.
accepted_answers: end annexation / unity of Christians and Muslims / clandestine preparation
questions.marking_points: 1 mark independence/anti-annexation; 1 mark Christian–Muslim unity; 1 mark clandestine urban organisation (not yet ELF army).
tips: ELM is political/secret; ELF is the later armed front.

questions.stem: What was the uniqueness of Manchester Pan-Africanism (6th) of 1945?
questions.answer: The 1945 Manchester Congress was dominated by Africans (not mainly diaspora intellectuals), demanded immediate independence rather than gradual reform, and linked Pan-Africanism to mass parties and trade unions. Future leaders such as Nkrumah and Kenyatta attended.
accepted_answers: African-led; immediate independence; future heads of state present
explanation_steps: Earlier congresses were elite/diaspora; 1945 turned to Africa itself
questions.marking_points: 1 mark African (not only diaspora) leadership; 1 mark demand for immediate independence; 1 mark presence of future leaders / mass politics.

questions.stem: Mention the success and failure of the American War of Independence.
questions.answer: Success: the Thirteen Colonies won independence (1783), wrote a republican constitution and inspired later revolutions. Failure/limits: slavery continued, Native Americans lost land, women and the poor were excluded from power, and loyalists were displaced.
explanation_steps: Answer: independence succeeded; equality did not
questions.marking_points: 1.5 marks any two successes (independence, constitution, inspiration); 1.5 marks any two limits (slavery, Natives, limited franchise).
tips: Always give both a win and a limit.

questions.stem: List the five Eritrean towns that remained under enemy control in 1977.
questions.answer: In the 1977 strategic offensive the EPLF/ELF took most towns; five that stayed under the Derg included Assab, Barentu, Adi Quala, Tesseney/Aligider area variations appear in sources — the standard school list is Assab, Barentu, Adi Quala, and two of: Teseney, Nakfa was already EPLF, Massawa still contested. Common textbook five: Assab, Massawa, Barentu, Adi Quala, and Tesseney (or Adi Keyih). Flag for review.
explanation_steps: 1977 towns still held by the Derg after the first liberation wave
Answer: Assab, Massawa, Barentu, Adi Quala, Tesseney
questions.marking_points: 0.6 each for any five accepted towns from: Assab, Massawa, Barentu, Adi Quala, Tesseney, Adi Keyih, Mendefera.
tips: Port towns Assab and Massawa stayed longest.
questions.review_flag: School lists of the five 1977 garrison towns vary; accepted a set of common names.
